checks.why: a call through an interface-typed receiver is a caller of the interface member, and every implementation must change with it; a call on a freshly constructed receiver binds to the class and is not a caller of the interface, and a same-named method on an unrelated class is not an implementation
an implementation is bound to the interface member it implements
a call through an abstract-class receiver is a caller of the abstract method, and its override must change with it
